label: early-position h/1/2/l input (weak, diffuse token+position code)
explanation: Diffuse unit, active on about 5% of steps. It favours the input tokens h, 1, 2 and l (in_tok rates 16-28% against a 5% base) and early positions: t=0 has 2.7x lift, and rate falls through the original phase. A second bump sits on the first copy-phase input (recall_idx=1, where the input is orig(0)), which also holds most of the top activations, e.g. a re-fed first token like h, j, 1 or k right after <DEL>. Activation is also elevated at copy steps 8-10. The best simple predicate (h/1/2/l input at t<=3) reaches only about 0.5 precision and 0.42 recall (dev F1 0.46, mass recall 0.45). Adding the recall_idx==1 step or more tokens trades precision for recall without passing F1 0.45. Many activations are on other tokens at mid positions, and many h/1/2/l inputs at early positions stay inactive. No coherent single description captures most of the mass.
